findings.highlight: you're real nice too
findings.evidenceJa: 風格も十分
findings.governingReading: 風格 praises the commanding presence or dignity appropriate to Saber, following praise for her strategic answer.
findings.explanation: Rin’s assessment of Saber’s bearing becomes praise for being nice.

findings.highlight: There's definitely some screws loose in there.
findings.evidenceJa: あいつの頭の中、一度見てみたくなった
findings.governingReading: She says she has come to want a look inside his head after noting his indifference to magical roles.
findings.explanation: Rin’s curiosity about how Shirou thinks becomes a definite assertion that he has screws loose.

findings.highlight: The priest must be distinguished
findings.evidenceJa: ここの神父はよほどの人格者と見える
findings.governingReading: 人格者 evaluates good character, an ironic early estimate before meeting Kirei.
findings.explanation: Shirou infers exceptional moral character from the church; the English only infers distinction.

findings.highlight: behind the world's largest religion
findings.evidenceJa: 一大宗教の裏側
findings.governingReading: 一大宗教 says a major/great religion; it supplies no world ranking.
findings.explanation: A major religion becomes the world’s largest religion.

findings.highlight: You're good at that, right?
findings.evidenceJa: そういう追い込み得意でしょ
findings.governingReading: Rin identifies putting someone under pressure or cornering them as Kotomine's specialty.
findings.explanation: Rin's remark about Kotomine's skill at cornering people becomes praise for elementary instruction. His subsequent pressure remains, but her pointed recognition of it disappears.

findings.highlight: the cleansing of your soul from the filth of this world
findings.evidenceJa: その裡に溜まった泥を全て掻き出す事もできる
findings.governingReading: The source offers to scrape out the mud accumulated within him, then erase invisible burn scars. It does not identify external worldly contamination or promise to erase a hidden entity that burned him.
findings.explanation: Kirei’s imagery of inner accumulated damage is recast as purification from worldly filth and erasing an unseen cause.

findings.highlight: such pity is unbecoming
findings.evidenceJa: 情けは人の為ならず
findings.governingReading: Kindness is not solely for the other person: it returns to benefit the giver. Rin asks whether he benefits and Kirei explicitly answers that helping others saves oneself.
findings.explanation: The self-benefit proverb becomes a claim that pity is unbecoming.

findings.highlight: If I squint I might be able to see it like that
findings.evidenceJa: 賭けてもいいが
findings.governingReading: 賭けてもいいが introduces his confidence that the priest does not consider it a trial at all.
findings.explanation: Shirou’s I-would-bet certainty becomes a concession that he could see the war as a trial.

findings.highlight: Even if it did exist, the Holy Grail is an imaginary power impossible to replicate.
findings.evidenceJa: 実在したとも、再現できたとも聞かない
findings.governingReading: Shirou says he has never heard of its actual existence or successful reproduction.
findings.explanation: Lack of reports of a real or reproduced Grail becomes impossibility of replication.

findings.highlight: an amateur or a coward
findings.evidenceJa: 半人前どころか、ただの腑抜け
findings.governingReading: どころか rejects the weaker amateur assessment as inadequate and escalates to spineless coward.
findings.explanation: Kirei’s escalation beyond amateur to coward becomes two alternative labels.

findings.highlight: part of the lowest-ranked special agencies
findings.evidenceJa: 特務局の末端
findings.governingReading: 末端 describes this church’s position as an outlying/end branch of the bureau tasked with relic recovery.
findings.explanation: A peripheral branch of a special bureau becomes membership in lowest-ranked special agencies.

findings.highlight: That fire is what remains of the previous Holy Grail War.
findings.evidenceJa: 未だ以て原因不明とされるあの火災
findings.governingReading: 未だ以て原因不明とされる contrasts its still-unexplained public status with Kirei’s revelation that it traces to the war.
findings.explanation: The fire’s continuing public classification as unexplained is omitted.

findings.highlight: Such disasterous misfortune does not happen every time.
findings.evidenceJa: そう毎回全滅などという憂き目は起きん
findings.governingReading: 全滅 names every participant being wiped out; he is answering whether someone has obtained the Grail in earlier wars.
findings.explanation: Kirei’s assurance that total annihilation does not occur every time becomes unspecified disastrous misfortune.

findings.highlight: you may do so any day of the week.
findings.evidenceJa: 私は毎日触れているぞ
findings.governingReading: 私は is Kirei: he uses his own routine handling as an example of merely taking the vessel in hand.
findings.explanation: Kirei’s statement that he touches the vessel daily becomes permission for Shirou to touch it any day.

findings.highlight: All due to the folly of one man's foolishness.
findings.evidenceJa: つまらぬ感傷に流された結果
findings.governingReading: 感傷に流される describes yielding to emotion/sentiment; つまらぬ is his contemptuous judgment.
findings.explanation: Kirei’s blame of sentimental weakness becomes a generic accusation of foolishness.

findings.highlight: I did up to the halfway point.
findings.evidenceJa: 途中まで戦いはした
findings.governingReading: 途中まで means up to some intermediate point; 真っ先 says he was first among the competitors to lose his Servant.
findings.explanation: Indefinite partial participation and being first to lose a Servant become an exact halfway point and immediate loss.

findings.highlight: I'll face this on my pride as a mage.
findings.evidenceJa: その言葉に恥じないよう、胸を張って進む
findings.governingReading: He has said as a man that he will fight; from here he must proceed without disgracing those words.
findings.explanation: Shirou’s duty to honor his spoken commitment becomes pride in being a mage.

findings.highlight: And so on and so forth.
findings.evidenceJa: あとはそう大差はない
findings.governingReading: そう大差はない says the rest do not differ greatly, in the question about summoning order/time.
findings.explanation: The remaining summons’ close timing is replaced with an empty continuation phrase.

findings.highlight: you are forced to listen to a lecture
findings.evidenceJa: つまらない論議の末
findings.governingReading: 連中は...論議の末...奪い取る has the Church confiscate the Grail after its discussion/debate.
findings.explanation: The Church’s tedious deliberations become a lecture Rin is forced to hear.

findings.highlight: The grounds seems to cover
findings.evidenceJa: 高台のほとんどを敷地にしているのか
findings.governingReading: English agreement errors occur independently of the Japanese meaning.
findings.explanation: Plural and compound subjects repeatedly take singular verbs, and a singular subject takes a plural verb.

findings.highlight: It's not like feel any hostility
findings.evidenceJa: 言峰という男に敵意を感じる訳でもない
findings.governingReading: The source clauses are complete; the English missing words obstruct ordinary sentence construction.
findings.explanation: Necessary subjects, auxiliaries, articles or idiom objects are missing in several complete English clauses.

findings.highlight: disasterous misfortune
findings.evidenceJa: 全滅などという憂き目
findings.governingReading: Disastrous, nuisance and official have standard spellings; the duplicated too is not source repetition.
findings.explanation: Repeated misspellings and an accidental repeated word remain in the English text.

findings.highlight: I can't thank you enough, Shirou Emiya.
findings.evidenceJa: 衛宮士郎には感謝をしてもし足りない
findings.governingReading: The complete Japanese speech remains within one opening and closing dialogue bracket.
findings.explanation: Dialogue quotes are missing or close prematurely within Kirei’s continuous speech.
